look_here_first: INTRODUCED wild oat: a loose, open, often dangling panicle with large narrow hanging multi-flowered spikelets, each commonly with long knee-bent/twisted awns. Check callus hairs, two glumes and individual fertile lemma awn under a lens. Its drooping spikelet looks like oats, but cannot identify A. fatua versus cultivated oats without mature florets.

crew_field_check: Compare cultivated Avena sativa (oat)—often less disarticulation/hairiness and fewer conspicuous twisted awns. Hordeum and Secale have compact central spikes rather than a loose dangling oat panicle. Treat as introduced, not a native Hays County grass.
Confirm true collar, ripe spikelets and habit from the same source-identified individual.
